{{nihongo|'''Washizu Shrine'''|鷲頭神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

=== Overview ===
It is enshrined on a small hill (Tenman-yama) at the tip of the southern foothills of Ōhira-yama, at the south end of the Ōhira area between the {{ill|Shizuura Mountains|arz|جبال شيزورا|ja|静浦山地|lld|Crëps de Shizuura|qid=Q11663639}} and the {{ill|Kano River|arz|نهر كانو|ceb|Kano-gawa|de|Kano (Fluss)|fa|رود کانو|fr|Kano-gawa|ha|Kogin Kano|ig|Osimiri Kano|ja|狩野川|ru|Кано (река)|th|แม่น้ำคาโนะ|zh|狩野川|qid=Q6364188}}, at the eastern edge of Numazu.

Also, on the summit of {{ill|Mount Washizu|Q11676307|qid=Q11676307}} to the southwest from there stands a small shrine as the Okumiya.

It is sometimes proposed as a candidate for Ōasa Shrine, a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, but this is not considered likely because shrine tradition states that it was founded by inviting {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takaokami-no-Kami}}, a water deity, from a shrine in Iyo in {{ill|Bunmei|fa|بونمئی|fr|Ère Bunmei|ia|Bunmei|ja|文明 (日本)|ko|분메이|ru|Буммэй|simple|Bunmei|sr|Бунмеи|sv|Bunmei|th|บุมเม|tr|Bunmei|zh|文明 (日本)|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} 1 ({{ill|1469|ab|1469|af|1469|als|1469|am|1469 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1469|ar|1469|ary|1469|arz|1469|ast|1469|avk|1469|az|1469|azb|۱۴۶۹ (میلادی)|be|1469|be_x_old|1469|bg|1469|bn|১৪৬৯|bpy|মারি ১৪৬৯|br|1469|bs|1469.|ca|1469|cdo|1469 nièng|ce|1469 шо|ceb|1469|ckb|١٤٦٩|crh|1469|cs|1469|cv|1469|cy|1469|da|1469|de|1469|diq|1469|el|1469|eml|1469|eo|1469|es|1469|et|1469|eu|1469|fa|۱۴۶۹ (میلادی)|fi|1469|fo|1469|fr|1469|frr|1469|fy|1469|ga|1469|gan|1469年|gcr|1469|gd|1469|gl|1469|gv|1469|he|1469|hi|१४६९|hif|1469|hr|1469.|ht|1469 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1469|hy|1469|ia|1469|id|1469|ilo|1469|io|1469|is|1469|it|1469|ja|1469年|jv|1469|ka|1469|kaa|1469|kk|1469 жыл|ko|1469년|la|1469|lb|1469|li|1469|lij|1469|lmo|1469|lt|1469 m.|lv|1469. gads|mai|१४६९|map_bms|1469|mdf|1469|mhr|1469|mi|1469|min|1469|mk|1469|mr|इ.स. १४६९|mrj|1469 и|ms|1469|my|၁၄၆၉|myv|1469 ие|mzn|۱۴۶۹|nah|1469|nap|1469|nds|1469|new|सन् १४६९|nl|1469|nn|1469|no|1469|nrm|1469|nso|1469|oc|1469|or|୧୪୬୯|os|1469-æм аз|pl|1469|pnb|1469|pt|1469|qu|1469|ro|1469|ru|1469 год|rue|1469|sa|१४६९|sah|1469|scn|1469|sd|1469ع|se|1469|sh|1469.|shn|1469|simple|1469|sk|1469|sl|1469|smn|1469|sq|1469|sr|1469|su|1469|sv|1469|sw|1469|ta|1469|te|1469|tg|Соли 1469|th|พ.ศ. 2012|tk|1469|tl|1469|tly|1469|tr|1469|tt|1469 ел|uk|1469|ur|1469ء|uz|1469|vec|1469|vi|1469|vls|1469|wa|1469|war|1469|wuu|1469年|xmf|1469|yi|1469|zea|1469|zh|1469年|zh_min_nan|1469 nî|zh_yue|1469年|qid=Q6566}}) for prayers regarding flood control and drought<ref name="gen">[https://genbu.net/data/izu/wasidu_title.htm 鷲頭神社] - Genshōshi</ref><ref name="engi">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140212-05.html 鷲頭神社] - Research on Engishiki Shrines</ref>.

It is said that at first it stood beside Kannondō in Togaya at the foothills of Mt. Washizu, a little southwest of the current site, but in Bunmei 13 ({{ill|1481|Q6631|qid=Q6631}}) it was moved to the summit of Mt. Washisu<ref name="engi"/>.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 7 ({{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}}), it was moved to the summit of Tenman-yama, its current location, and Tenjin Shrine and village shrines were merged; in Meiji 8 ({{ill|1875|Q7764|qid=Q7764}}), it was ranked as a village shrine<ref name="engi"/>.
